newsitem.title: UK: Lloyd's 1995 insurance profit little changed-Chats.
newsitem.headline: Lloyd's 1995 insurance profit little changed-Chats.

text.p: Lloyd's insurance market is heading for a virtually unchanged profit of 936 million stg on its 1995 year of account, commentator Chatset said on Friday.
This compares with a 1994 profit of 913 million stg for Lloyd's, which publishes its results three years in arrears to allow for the settlement of most claims.
Chatset's latest forecast for the 1995 year, published in its 1994 Lloyd's League Tables Part 1, is slightly lower than its January forecast of 1.008 billion stg.
This reflects a deterioration on the Lloyd's non-marine result and a move into loss for motor insurers.
Lloyd's own forecast for 1995 is an unchanged 913 million stg.
Chatset has also revised its 1996 profit forecast slightly lower to 706 million stg from its January estimate of 717 million. Lloyd's own forecast is a profit of 600 million stg.
Chatset, which is owned by Lloyd's members' agent LRG Cater Allen, specialises in analysing and forecasting the performance of Lloyd's underwriting syndicates.
The latest edition of its League Tables concentrates on syndicates planning to trade forward into 1998. Part 2 will review other syndicates.
